duplicates.title: [PRD-03] Organizations and Organization Membership
duplicates.body:
## Implementation ticket

Implements **PRD-03** from the approved StrataAI requirements.

### Adopted StrataAI2 architecture
- React + TypeScript + Vite + **MUI/Material UI**; MUI is the primary UI/styling system.
- `dnd-kit` for accessible Kanban drag/drop where applicable.
- ASP.NET Core modular monolith with `Domain`, `Application`, `Infrastructure`, `Api`, and separate `Worker` process projects.
- PostgreSQL + RLS; pgvector for semantic retrieval where required.
- Object storage for binaries; SignalR for realtime collaboration.
- PostgreSQL-backed durable jobs/transactional outbox initially.
- CI builds immutable web/API/Worker Docker images once and emits the tested images.

# PRD-03 — Organizations and Organization Membership

## 1. PRD Identifier
**PRD-03**

## 2. Feature Name
**Organizations and Organization Membership**

## 3. Executive Summary
Defines organization creation, editing, membership, roles, invitations, board directory, leave/delete behavior, and organization-level governance.

## 4. Problem Statement
A Trello-class collaborative Kanban product appears simple at the surface but depends on precise domain rules, authorization, lifecycle semantics, concurrency controls, and predictable interaction behavior. This PRD defines the behavior required for **Organizations and Organization Membership** without relying on proprietary implementation details.

## 5. Product Objective
Deliver a testable, production-oriented implementation of this domain that integrates consistently with the canonical Organization → Board → List → Card model.

## 6. User Personas
- **Organization Owner/Admin** — governs membership and organization-level configuration.
- **Board Admin** — manages board-level collaboration and controls.
- **Contributor** — creates and changes work items.
- **Viewer** — inspects content without mutation rights.
- **Public Visitor** — may inspect PUBLIC boards only where permitted.

## 7. User Stories
- As a user, I can create a organization.
- As a user, I can invite and remove members.
- As a user, I can see all boards in a organization.
- As a user, I can leave or delete a organization when authorized.

## 8. Functional Requirements
- **WS-FR-001** — Authenticated users SHALL be able to create a organization.
- **WS-FR-002** — Organization fields SHALL include name, description, logo/avatar, owner, status, createdAt, updatedAt.
- **WS-FR-003** — Organization admins SHALL be able to rename and edit organization metadata.
- **WS-FR-004** — Authorized users SHALL be able to invite members by email.
- **WS-FR-005** — Organization admins SHALL be able to remove members subject to ownership safeguards.
- **WS-FR-006** — Members SHALL be able to leave a organization unless they are the sole owner/admin required for continuity.
- **WS-FR-007** — The organization home SHALL list all boards the current user is authorized to discover.
- **WS-FR-008** — Organization roles SHALL include OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER.
- **WS-FR-009** — Deleting a organization SHALL require explicit confirmation and SHALL be restricted to authorized owners.
- **WS-FR-010** — Organization deletion SHALL define treatment of boards, lists, cards, attachments, and audit records.

## 9. Detailed Interaction Behaviour
- Changes should appear immediately using optimistic updates when rollback/reconciliation is safe.
- The server is authoritative for authorization, validation, version, and persisted state.
- Shared-state changes emit domain events and become visible to other authorized clients through the realtime layer.
- Destructive operations follow PRD-18 lifecycle rules.
- Controls unavailable to the user may be hidden/disabled for UX, but the same action must still be rejected server-side.

## 10. Business Rules
- Every board belongs to one organization.
- A organization must retain at least one owner until deletion.
- Invitation acceptance may require authentication or registration.

## 11. Permission Rules
- `VIEW`: depends on board/organization visibility and membership.
- `CREATE`: requires authenticated membership and the relevant create permission.
- `EDIT`: requires edit rights to the entity's board.
- `MOVE`: requires edit/move rights in both source and destination contexts where applicable.
- `COMMENT`: requires authenticated board participation unless future policy explicitly allows otherwise.
- `INVITE`: requires board/organization administrative rights.
- `ARCHIVE` / `RESTORE`: require edit or administrative rights according to entity policy.
- `DELETE`: requires elevated permission and lifecycle preconditions.
- `ADMINISTER`: limited to the relevant admin/owner role.
- Every permission is enforced on the server; UI state is never the security boundary.

## 12. Data Requirements
Organization, OrganizationMember, Invitation. Unique membership on (organizationId,userId). Invitation tokens unique and expiring.

All mutable records require `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. Concurrency-sensitive records require a version/revision field. Foreign-key or equivalent integrity checks must prevent cross-board/cross-organization inconsistencies.

## 13. API Requirements
POST /organizations; PATCH /organizations/{id}; DELETE /organizations/{id}; GET /organizations/{id}/boards; POST /organizations/{id}/invitations; DELETE /organizations/{id}/members/{userId}

General API rules:
- Schema-validate all input.
- Return consistent error envelopes.
- Enforce authorization before protected disclosure.
- Support idempotency for retry-prone mutations.
- Use cursor pagination for unbounded collections.
- Return updated entity version after successful concurrency-sensitive mutations.

## 14. Real-Time / Event Requirements
The following events are directly relevant:
- `ORGANIZATION_CREATED`
- `ORGANIZATION_UPDATED`
- `ORGANIZATION_MEMBER_INVITED`
- `ORGANIZATION_MEMBER_ADDED`
- `ORGANIZATION_MEMBER_REMOVED`
- `ORGANIZATION_DELETED`

Events must contain `eventId`, `eventType`, `actorId`, `organizationId`, `boardId`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `version` where relevant, `metadata`, and `createdAt`. Clients deduplicate by `eventId`.

## 15. UX Requirements
- Primary desktop interactions must remain fast and visually direct.
- All critical actions remain available on tablet and mobile web.
- Destructive actions require explicit confirmation.
- Empty/loading/error states must not shift the user into ambiguous contexts.
- The UI should preserve board scroll/list context when opening and closing card detail.

## 16. Accessibility Requirements
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
- All interactive controls require accessible names.
- Visible keyboard focus is mandatory.
- Pointer drag/drop has keyboard equivalent where movement is involved.
- Dialogs manage focus correctly.
- Color is never the sole status indicator.
- Realtime changes that affect the current operation use non-disruptive accessible announcements.

## 17. Error and Empty States
- Empty state: explain the next permitted action.
- Permission denied: state that access/action is unavailable without leaking protected metadata.
- Validation error: identify the affected field/action.
- Network timeout: preserve recoverable client state and offer retry.
- Conflict: reconcile to server state and explain that the item changed elsewhere.
- Deleted/missing entity: distinguish not-found from inaccessible only where doing so is safe.

## 18. Edge Cases
- Concurrent edits from multiple authorized clients.
- User loses permission while the entity is open.
- Parent board/list becomes archived during editing.
- Duplicate client submission after timeout.
- Realtime event arrives before mutation response.
- Realtime event is missed during disconnect and recovered later.
- Entity is moved while another user is viewing its detail.
- Very large boards requiring virtualization.

## 19. Non-Functional Requirements
- Board initial usable rendering target: **<1.5 s** under documented normal conditions.
- Simple movement visual feedback target: **<100 ms**.
- Server mutation acknowledgement target: **p95 <500 ms**.
- Cached card-detail opening target: **<200 ms**.
- Design supports at least **200 lists/board**, **5,000 cards/board**, and **100,000 archived cards/organization**.
- Log errors with correlation IDs but avoid logging sensitive content bodies by default.

## 20. Analytics / Telemetry
Track:
- feature open/use counts;
- mutation latency and success/failure;
- permission denials by stable error code;
- realtime reconnect/conflict rates;
- client exceptions;
- user-visible retry events.
Do not use analytics events as the source of truth for audit history.

## 21. Dependencies
- PRD-02
- PRD-05
- PRD-18

## 22. Out of Scope
Cross-organization administration, billing, public template marketplace.

## 23. Acceptance Criteria
**AC-WS-03-01**
GIVEN an authorized user is using this feature
WHEN the user performs the primary supported action associated with WS-FR-001
THEN the server validates authorization and input
AND the resulting state is persisted
AND the client reflects the authoritative result.

**AC-WS-03-02**
GIVEN the same operation would violate the rule represented by WS-FR-003
WHEN the user or client attempts the operation
THEN the server rejects it with a stable error code
AND protected state is unchanged
AND no unauthorized information is disclosed.

**AC-WS-03-03**
GIVEN two clients have the same board or entity open
WHEN a successful mutation relevant to WS-FR-010 occurs
THEN the initiating client receives confirmation
AND other authorized clients receive or recover the updated state without requiring a full manual reload.

## 24. Test Scenarios
1. Primary happy path.
2. Empty-state behavior.
3. Invalid input.
4. Unauthorized user.
5. User loses permission mid-session.
6. Network timeout and retry.
7. Duplicate request/idempotency.
8. Two-client concurrent update.
9. Realtime disconnect/reconnect recovery.
10. Archived/deleted parent behavior.
11. Keyboard-only operation.
12. Mobile viewport.
13. Large-data performance case where applicable.

## 25. Definition of Done
- All functional requirements implemented.
- Server-side authorization tests pass.
- Schema and migration changes reviewed.
- Domain events emitted and consumed where required.
- Unit, integration, and end-to-end tests pass.
- Accessibility checks and keyboard scenarios pass.
- Error/empty/loading states are implemented.
- Telemetry is documented.
- No known P0/P1 defects.
- Product behavior is documented sufficiently that another team does not need to invent missing core rules.

## 26. Open Questions
- Any unresolved implementation choice discovered during development must be recorded explicitly.
- If a choice changes cross-PRD behavior, the affected PRDs and traceability mappings must be updated before release.

---

## Linked test cases
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-01** — Primary happy path.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-02** — Empty-state behavior.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-03** — Invalid input.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-04** — Unauthorized user.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-05** — User loses permission mid-session.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-06** — Network timeout and retry.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-07** — Duplicate request/idempotency.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-08** — Two-client concurrent update.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-09** — Realtime disconnect/reconnect recovery.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-10** — Archived/deleted parent behavior.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-11** — Keyboard-only operation.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-12** — Mobile viewport.
- [ ] **PRD-03-TC-13** — Large-data performance case where applicable.

## Agent execution contract
- Implement all PRD requirements and acceptance criteria; do not silently narrow scope.
- Preserve Organization/tenant isolation and the separate Owner Portal authorization surface.
- Add/update automated tests before closure and reference the PRD/AC/test IDs in code or traceability metadata.
- Include migrations, authorization, events, audit, accessibility, concurrency, errors/empty states, and observability where required.
- Link the implementation pull request to this issue and include executed test evidence.
- Do not add a datastore, broker, framework, or deployable service without an approved architecture decision.

definitions.title: [ARCH-01] Repository, Solution and Technology Baseline
definitions.body:
## Architecture implementation ticket

This architecture ticket is binding across the StrataAI2 functional PRDs.

### Adopted StrataAI2 override
Use a monorepo with `apps/web`, `src/StrataAI.Domain`, `src/StrataAI.Application`, `src/StrataAI.Infrastructure`, `src/StrataAI.Api`, `src/StrataAI.Worker`, and test projects. React + TypeScript + Vite + **MUI/Material UI** is the frontend baseline; Tailwind is not the primary styling system.

# ARCH-01 — Repository, Solution and Technology Baseline

## 1. PRD identifier
ARCH-01

## 2. Feature name
Repository, Solution and Technology Baseline

## 3. Executive summary
Preserve the StrataBCAI monorepo and technology pattern as the baseline for the new StrataAI.

## 4. Problem statement
The expanded StrataAI functional suite requires a stable architecture contract. Without one, teams or coding agents could choose incompatible frameworks, data-access patterns, security boundaries, runtime modes, or release mechanisms.

## 5. Product objective
Provide one reproducible repository and technology baseline for all 80 functional PRDs.

## 6. User personas
- Software developer
- Technical architect
- DevOps/release engineer
- Security/privacy reviewer
- System administrator
- Quality engineer

## 7. User stories
- As a developer, I know exactly where this capability belongs and which interfaces it must use.
- As a release engineer, I can reproduce the same build locally and in CI.
- As a security reviewer, I can identify the trust and tenant boundaries.
- As an operator, I can run, diagnose, upgrade, and roll back the application.

## 8. Functional requirements
- **ARCH-01-FR-001** — The repository SHALL be a monorepo with `apps/web`, `src/StrataAI.Api`, `tests/StrataAI.Api.Tests`, `.github/workflows`, `docs`, `scripts`, and root Docker/Compose assets.
- **ARCH-01-FR-002** — The web baseline SHALL be React 19+, TypeScript 5.9+, Vite 7+, and Tailwind CSS 4+ unless a major-version ADR changes it.
- **ARCH-01-FR-003** — The API baseline SHALL be ASP.NET Core/.NET 10 with nullable reference types and warnings treated as errors.
- **ARCH-01-FR-004** — Production persistence SHALL use PostgreSQL 17+ through Npgsql.
- **ARCH-01-FR-005** — The production web runtime SHALL be Nginx serving static SPA assets and proxying `/api` to the API container.
- **ARCH-01-FR-006** — Top-level package/build commands SHALL expose build, test, typecheck, and lint for CI.
- **ARCH-01-FR-007** — Dependencies SHALL be reproducibly locked; CI SHOULD use lockfile-based installs such as `npm ci`.
- **ARCH-01-FR-008** — Major runtime/framework changes SHALL require an ADR and explicit CI validation.
- **ARCH-01-FR-009** — Functional domains SHALL remain modules in the modular monolith unless a future approved architecture decision extracts them.
- **ARCH-01-FR-010** — Domain-facing terminology SHALL use Organization; `tenant_id` is permitted only as infrastructure terminology.

## 9. Detailed interaction behaviour
All components must interact through the interfaces and trust boundaries defined by this PRD. Internal convenience must never bypass Organization isolation, authorization, audit, versioning, or provider boundaries.

## 10. Business / architecture rules
- Organization is the canonical tenant/domain boundary.
- `tenant_id` may be used as the infrastructure key representing an Organization.
- Production must fail closed rather than silently falling back to Demo behaviour.
- Build artifacts are immutable; environment-specific configuration is external.

## 11. Permission rules
Infrastructure must not broaden functional permissions. Authentication, Organization membership, Board permissions, governance roles, acting capacity, confidentiality, and owner-portal isolation remain server-authoritative.

## 12. Data requirements
Every tenant-owned persisted record must carry or be unambiguously scoped to an Organization/tenant. Schema constraints and indexes must enforce correctness where practical.

## 13. API requirements
APIs must use stable contracts, server-side authorization, consistent problem responses, idempotency where required, and explicit Organization context.

## 14. Real-time / event requirements
Events must preserve Organization context, correlation metadata, authorization-safe payloads, and stable event names. Event delivery must never expose data to an unauthorized subscriber.

## 15. UX requirements
Infrastructure states that affect users—Demo Mode, integration failure, stale version, degraded availability, pending AI processing—must have understandable and non-sensitive UI states.

## 16. Accessibility requirements
Architecture must preserve WCAG 2.2 AA capability. User-facing diagnostic or error states must be keyboard and screen-reader accessible.

## 17. Error and empty states
Fail closed on missing tenant/security configuration. Do not expose SQL, stack traces, secrets, provider credentials, or inaccessible-record existence.

## 18. Edge cases
Test missing configuration, dependency outage, container restart, partial deployment, stale client, duplicate/replayed integration messages, concurrent operations, failed migrations, and interrupted CI runs as applicable.

## 19. Non-functional requirements
Security, tenant isolation, deterministic builds, maintainability, observability, reproducibility, recoverability, and least privilege are mandatory.

## 20. Analytics / telemetry
Structured logs, metrics, traces, audit events, and build metadata must correlate failures and changes without recording secrets or prohibited personal data.

## 21. Dependencies
- PRD-01
- PRD-19
- PRD-21
- PRD-25
- PRD-26

## 22. Out of scope
- Native mobile applications
- Microservice decomposition by default

## 23. Acceptance criteria
- **ARCH-01-AC-001** — GIVEN a clean checkout WHEN documented toolchains are available THEN web and API build without undocumented prerequisites.
- **ARCH-01-AC-002** — GIVEN a green commit WHEN release assets are produced THEN web and API share the same commit-derived build identifier.
- **ARCH-01-AC-003** — GIVEN a new functional module WHEN added THEN it fits the monorepo/module boundaries without creating an ad-hoc deployable service.

## 24. Test scenarios
Automated tests must cover all acceptance criteria plus material negative/security paths. CI must execute the tests relevant to this architecture boundary.

## 25. Definition of done
- All functional requirements are implemented or resolved by an approved ADR.
- Automated tests are green.
- CI validates the architecture boundary.
- Documentation matches the running system.
- No undocumented local-only dependency is required.

## 26. Open questions
- Whether .NET major upgrades are pinned manually or track future LTS releases.


---

---

## Linked test cases
- [x] **ARCH-01-TC-01** — Automated tests must cover all acceptance criteria plus material negative/security paths. CI must execute the tests relevant to this architecture boundary.

## Agent execution contract
- Treat this architecture ticket as a cross-cutting constraint for relevant PRD implementation tickets.
- Add automated tests for the acceptance criteria and reference ARCH/AC/test IDs.
- Do not silently substitute a different framework, datastore, message broker, deployment topology, authorization boundary, or CI release model.
- Link implementation PRs to this issue and include executed test evidence.

definitions.title: [ARCH-02] Web SPA, Nginx Edge and Front-End Module Architecture
definitions.body:
## Architecture implementation ticket

This architecture ticket is binding across the StrataAI2 functional PRDs.

### Adopted StrataAI2 override
Use **MUI/Material UI** as the authoritative component system, MUI X Community where useful, and `dnd-kit` for Kanban drag/drop. Use MUI theme/`sx`/`styled()` rather than a competing Tailwind-first styling model. Internal Council/Management and Owner Portal remain separate route/layout/security surfaces in the same SPA.

# ARCH-02 — Web SPA, Nginx Edge and Front-End Module Architecture

## 1. PRD identifier
ARCH-02

## 2. Feature name
Web SPA, Nginx Edge and Front-End Module Architecture

## 3. Executive summary
The browser application is a React/TypeScript/Vite SPA served by Nginx, preserving the reference deployment pattern while using stronger feature modularity for the expanded product.

## 4. Problem statement

## 6. User personas
- Software developer
- Technical architect
- DevOps/release engineer
- Security/privacy reviewer
- System administrator
- Quality engineer

- As a security reviewer, I can identify the trust and tenant boundaries.
- As an operator, I can run, diagnose, upgrade, and roll back the application.

- **ARCH-02-FR-001** — The web SHALL be a client-side React SPA built by Vite.
- **ARCH-02-FR-002** — The production image SHALL serve compiled assets with Nginx and use SPA fallback routing.
- **ARCH-02-FR-003** — Nginx SHALL reverse-proxy `/api/` to service name `api` over the private container/deployment network.
- **ARCH-02-FR-004** — Production domain state SHALL be obtained from typed API clients/services; browser localStorage SHALL NOT be the production system of record.
- **ARCH-02-FR-005** — Feature code SHALL be organized by domain (kanban, meetings, governance, operations, projects, documents, communications, AI, owner portal, settings) with shared UI primitives separated.
- **ARCH-02-FR-006** — The internal Council/Management surface and Owner Portal SHALL have separate route/layout/authorization surfaces even if delivered in one SPA build.
- **ARCH-02-FR-007** — The build SHALL inject a visible/supportable build identifier derived from CI commit/release metadata.
- **ARCH-02-FR-008** — Global state SHALL be limited to cross-cutting concerns such as authenticated user, active Organization, notifications, and shared query/cache state.
- **ARCH-02-FR-009** — API problems SHALL be normalized through one client error layer.
- **ARCH-02-FR-010** — Web tests SHALL use Vitest and React Testing Library; critical workflows SHALL use Playwright or equivalent end-to-end automation.

All components must interact through the interfaces and trust boundaries defined by this PRD. Internal convenience must never bypass Organization isolation, authorization, audit, versioning, or provider boundaries.

## 13. API requirements

## 14. Real-time / event requirements

## 15. UX requirements
Infrastructure states that affect users—Demo Mode, integration failure, stale version, degraded availability, pending AI processing—must have understandable and non-sensitive UI states.

## 16. Accessibility requirements
Architecture must preserve WCAG 2.2 AA capability. User-facing diagnostic or error states must be keyboard and screen-reader accessible.

## 17. Error and empty states

## 18. Edge cases
Test missing configuration, dependency outage, container restart, partial deployment, stale client, duplicate/replayed integration messages, concurrent operations, failed migrations, and interrupted CI runs as applicable.

## 19. Non-functional requirements

## 20. Analytics / telemetry

## 21. Dependencies
- ARCH-01
- ARCH-03
- ARCH-06
- ARCH-10
- PRD-80

## 22. Out of scope
- SSR as a mandatory requirement
- Direct browser-to-database access

## 23. Acceptance criteria
- **ARCH-02-AC-001** — GIVEN a deep SPA URL WHEN loaded directly THEN Nginx returns the SPA and the route resolves.
- **ARCH-02-AC-002** — GIVEN `/api/health` requested through the web origin THEN Nginx proxies to the API successfully.
- **ARCH-02-AC-003** — GIVEN an Owner Portal identity WHEN navigating THEN internal Council routes are not exposed and APIs independently reject them.
- **ARCH-02-AC-004** — GIVEN a CI build WHEN deployed THEN the UI reports the matching build identifier.

## 24. Test scenarios
Automated tests must cover all acceptance criteria plus material negative/security paths. CI must execute the tests relevant to this architecture boundary.

- Automated tests are green.
- CI validates the architecture boundary.
- Documentation matches the running system.

definitions.title: [ARCH-03] ASP.NET Core Modular-Monolith API Architecture
definitions.body:
## Architecture implementation ticket

This architecture ticket is binding across the StrataAI2 functional PRDs.

### Adopted StrataAI2 override
The modular monolith has two runtime process types from the same codebase: `StrataAI.Api` for HTTP/auth/realtime and `StrataAI.Worker` for email, AI, indexing, notifications, scheduled and durable jobs. Domain must not depend on ASP.NET, PostgreSQL, email/AI SDKs, or Docker.

definitions.title: [ARCH-04] PostgreSQL Persistence, Tenant Isolation and Schema Evolution
definitions.body:
## Architecture implementation ticket

This architecture ticket is binding across the StrataAI2 functional PRDs.

### Adopted StrataAI2 override
Use PostgreSQL as the primary datastore, PostgreSQL RLS as defence in depth, **pgvector** for semantic retrieval, and ordered versioned migrations. PostgreSQL also hosts transactional outbox/job metadata initially. Do not add MongoDB, Elasticsearch, or a separate vector database without measured need and an ADR.

# ARCH-04 — PostgreSQL Persistence, Tenant Isolation and Schema Evolution

## 1. PRD identifier
ARCH-04

## 2. Feature name
PostgreSQL Persistence, Tenant Isolation and Schema Evolution

## 3. Executive summary
Use PostgreSQL through Npgsql with application tenant checks and PostgreSQL RLS as defence in depth, while adding disciplined versioned migrations for the larger product.

## 4. Problem statement
The expanded StrataAI functional suite requires a stable architecture contract. Without one, teams or coding agents could choose incompatible frameworks, data-access patterns, security boundaries, runtime modes, or release mechanisms.

## 5. Product objective
Provide durable multi-Organization persistence that cannot leak data across tenants and can evolve safely through CI and deployment.

## 6. User personas
- Software developer
- Technical architect
- DevOps/release engineer
- Security/privacy reviewer
- System administrator
- Quality engineer

## 7. User stories
- As a developer, I know exactly where this capability belongs and which interfaces it must use.
- As a release engineer, I can reproduce the same build locally and in CI.
- As a security reviewer, I can identify the trust and tenant boundaries.
- As an operator, I can run, diagnose, upgrade, and roll back the application.

## 8. Functional requirements
- **ARCH-04-FR-001** — Production SHALL use PostgreSQL 17+ through Npgsql.
- **ARCH-04-FR-002** — Every tenant-owned table SHALL carry a non-null `tenant_id`/Organization isolation key unless demonstrably global.
- **ARCH-04-FR-003** — Every tenant-owned production query SHALL require explicit tenant context.
- **ARCH-04-FR-004** — PostgreSQL RLS SHALL be enabled and forced on tenant-owned tables where technically applicable.
- **ARCH-04-FR-005** — Database access SHALL set transaction-local/application-local tenant context before RLS-protected operations.
- **ARCH-04-FR-006** — Missing/malformed/unauthorized tenant context SHALL fail closed.
- **ARCH-04-FR-007** — Schema evolution SHALL use ordered, versioned migrations; a single ever-growing bootstrap SQL string SHALL NOT be the long-term migration mechanism.
- **ARCH-04-FR-008** — Migrations SHALL be idempotent where appropriate and backward-safe for rollback/promotion strategies where feasible.
- **ARCH-04-FR-009** — Append-only audit storage SHALL reject ordinary UPDATE/DELETE.
- **ARCH-04-FR-010** — Core domain entities SHALL use normalized tables/constraints/indexes where correctness and queryability require it; JSONB MAY be used for flexible metadata/version snapshots.
- **ARCH-04-FR-011** — Production startup SHALL verify schema compatibility before accepting traffic.
- **ARCH-04-FR-012** — CI SHALL test migrations and RLS against a real ephemeral PostgreSQL instance.

## 9. Detailed interaction behaviour
All components must interact through the interfaces and trust boundaries defined by this PRD. Internal convenience must never bypass Organization isolation, authorization, audit, versioning, or provider boundaries.

## 10. Business / architecture rules
- Organization is the canonical tenant/domain boundary.
- `tenant_id` may be used as the infrastructure key representing an Organization.
- Production must fail closed rather than silently falling back to Demo behaviour.
- Build artifacts are immutable; environment-specific configuration is external.

## 11. Permission rules
Infrastructure must not broaden functional permissions. Authentication, Organization membership, Board permissions, governance roles, acting capacity, confidentiality, and owner-portal isolation remain server-authoritative.

## 12. Data requirements
Every tenant-owned persisted record must carry or be unambiguously scoped to an Organization/tenant. Schema constraints and indexes must enforce correctness where practical.

## 13. API requirements
APIs must use stable contracts, server-side authorization, consistent problem responses, idempotency where required, and explicit Organization context.

## 14. Real-time / event requirements
Events must preserve Organization context, correlation metadata, authorization-safe payloads, and stable event names. Event delivery must never expose data to an unauthorized subscriber.

## 15. UX requirements
Infrastructure states that affect users—Demo Mode, integration failure, stale version, degraded availability, pending AI processing—must have understandable and non-sensitive UI states.

## 16. Accessibility requirements
Architecture must preserve WCAG 2.2 AA capability. User-facing diagnostic or error states must be keyboard and screen-reader accessible.

## 17. Error and empty states
Fail closed on missing tenant/security configuration. Do not expose SQL, stack traces, secrets, provider credentials, or inaccessible-record existence.

## 18. Edge cases
Test missing configuration, dependency outage, container restart, partial deployment, stale client, duplicate/replayed integration messages, concurrent operations, failed migrations, and interrupted CI runs as applicable.

## 19. Non-functional requirements
Security, tenant isolation, deterministic builds, maintainability, observability, reproducibility, recoverability, and least privilege are mandatory.

## 20. Analytics / telemetry
Structured logs, metrics, traces, audit events, and build metadata must correlate failures and changes without recording secrets or prohibited personal data.

## 21. Dependencies
- ARCH-03
- ARCH-06
- ARCH-09
- ARCH-12
- PRD-20
- PRD-70

## 22. Out of scope
- Database-per-tenant as the default

- **ARCH-04-AC-001** — GIVEN Organizations A and B WHEN A queries tenant-owned data THEN no B record can be returned even in tested paths with weakened application predicates.
- **ARCH-04-AC-002** — GIVEN a clean database WHEN all migrations run THEN the expected schema is produced deterministically.
- **ARCH-04-AC-003** — GIVEN an older supported schema WHEN the new image starts THEN forward migration succeeds or traffic is refused.
- **ARCH-04-AC-004** — GIVEN an audit row WHEN ordinary update/delete SQL executes THEN PostgreSQL rejects the mutation.

## 24. Test scenarios
Automated tests must cover all acceptance criteria plus material negative/security paths. CI must execute the tests relevant to this architecture boundary.

## 25. Definition of done
- All functional requirements are implemented or resolved by an approved ADR.
- Automated tests are green.
- CI validates the architecture boundary.
- Documentation matches the running system.
- No undocumented local-only dependency is required.

- **ARCH-08-FR-004** — HTTP requests and async jobs SHALL propagate correlation IDs where meaningful.
- **ARCH-08-FR-005** — Material business/security/governance changes SHALL create append-only AuditEvents distinct from diagnostic logs.

- **ARCH-08-FR-007** — OpenTelemetry-compatible tracing SHOULD cover edge -> API -> database/integration calls without logging sensitive payloads.
- **ARCH-08-FR-008** — Baseline service objectives SHALL support at least Standard 99.5% availability/API p95 <=750ms/RPO <=24h/RTO <=8h and Enhanced 99.9%/<=400ms/RPO <=1h/RTO <=2h.

- **ARCH-08-FR-010** — AI/email dependency failure SHALL degrade safely while preserving core human workflows and source records.
- **ARCH-08-FR-011** — Health endpoints SHALL not reveal secrets or protected tenant information.
- **ARCH-08-FR-012** — Build/version metadata SHALL be queryable for support correlation.

## 9. Detailed interaction behaviour
All components must interact through the interfaces and trust boundaries defined by this PRD. Internal convenience must never bypass Organization isolation, authorization, audit, versioning, or provider boundaries.

## 10. Business / architecture rules
- Organization is the canonical tenant/domain boundary.
- `tenant_id` may be used as the infrastructure key representing an Organization.
- Production must fail closed rather than silently falling back to Demo behaviour.
- Build artifacts are immutable; environment-specific configuration is external.

## 11. Permission rules
Infrastructure must not broaden functional permissions. Authentication, Organization membership, Board permissions, governance roles, acting capacity, confidentiality, and owner-portal isolation remain server-authoritative.

## 12. Data requirements
Every tenant-owned persisted record must carry or be unambiguously scoped to an Organization/tenant. Schema constraints and indexes must enforce correctness where practical.

## 13. API requirements
APIs must use stable contracts, server-side authorization, consistent problem responses, idempotency where required, and explicit Organization context.

## 14. Real-time / event requirements
Events must preserve Organization context, correlation metadata, authorization-safe payloads, and stable event names. Event delivery must never expose data to an unauthorized subscriber.

## 15. UX requirements
Infrastructure states that affect users—Demo Mode, integration failure, stale version, degraded availability, pending AI processing—must have understandable and non-sensitive UI states.

## 16. Accessibility requirements
Architecture must preserve WCAG 2.2 AA capability. User-facing diagnostic or error states must be keyboard and screen-reader accessible.

## 17. Error and empty states
Fail closed on missing tenant/security configuration. Do not expose SQL, stack traces, secrets, provider credentials, or inaccessible-record existence.

## 18. Edge cases
Test missing configuration, dependency outage, container restart, partial deployment, stale client, duplicate/replayed integration messages, concurrent operations, failed migrations, and interrupted CI runs as applicable.

## 19. Non-functional requirements
Security, tenant isolation, deterministic builds, maintainability, observability, reproducibility, recoverability, and least privilege are mandatory.

## 20. Analytics / telemetry
Structured logs, metrics, traces, audit events, and build metadata must correlate failures and changes without recording secrets or prohibited personal data.

## 21. Dependencies
- ARCH-04
- ARCH-07
- ARCH-10
- ARCH-11
- PRD-53
- PRD-70

## 22. Out of scope
- Selecting a mandatory telemetry vendor

## 23. Acceptance criteria
- **ARCH-08-AC-001** — GIVEN a running API WHEN health is called THEN a stable non-sensitive success response is returned.
- **ARCH-08-AC-002** — GIVEN the mandatory production database is unavailable WHEN readiness is evaluated THEN the API is not ready.
- **ARCH-08-AC-003** — GIVEN AI/email outage WHEN core Cards/meetings are used THEN core functionality remains available unless directly dependent.
- **ARCH-08-AC-004** — GIVEN a security-sensitive mutation WHEN committed THEN an append-only audit event exists.

## 24. Test scenarios
Automated tests must cover all acceptance criteria plus material negative/security paths. CI must execute the tests relevant to this architecture boundary.

## 25. Definition of done
- All functional requirements are implemented or resolved by an approved ADR.
- Automated tests are green.
- CI validates the architecture boundary.
- Documentation matches the running system.
- No undocumented local-only dependency is required.

- Choose the initial telemetry backend/OpenTelemetry collector.
