- `dnd-kit` for accessible Kanban drag/drop where applicable.
- ASP.NET Core modular monolith with Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Api, and a separate Worker process.
- PostgreSQL + RLS; pgvector for semantic retrieval where required.
- Object storage for binaries; SignalR for realtime collaboration.
- PostgreSQL-backed durable jobs/transactional outbox initially.
- CI builds immutable web/API/Worker Docker images once and emits the tested images.

# PRD-64 — Bylaw Enforcement and Compliance Cases

## 1. PRD Identifier
**PRD-64**

## 2. Feature Name
**Bylaw Enforcement and Compliance Cases**

## 3. Executive Summary
Manage formal bylaw/compliance cases separately from ordinary Cards while preserving evidence, hearing and decision history.

## 4. Problem Statement
Strata operations combine ordinary work management with sensitive records, changing governance roles, formal decisions, external correspondence and long-lived history. Without explicit rules for **Bylaw Enforcement and Compliance Cases**, an implementation would be forced to invent lifecycle, data, permission and audit behavior, creating inconsistent or unsafe outcomes.

## 5. Product Objective
Deliver a production-ready implementation of **Bylaw Enforcement and Compliance Cases** that is Organization-scoped, permission-safe, auditable, accessible, and consistent with the canonical StrataAI model.

## 6. User Personas
- Organization Administrator — configures tenant-level policy and access.
- Council Member — performs governance and operational collaboration.
- President / Vice-President — performs council leadership tasks subject to explicit permissions.
- Strata Manager — acts professionally for assigned Organizations within delegated permissions.
- Property Management Company User — supports assigned manager/portfolio workflows.
- Owner / Resident — uses only the separated portal surface where invited.
- System / AI Service Actor — performs only explicitly authorized automated processing.

## 7. User Stories
- As an authorized user, I can use bylaw enforcement and compliance cases without bypassing Organization or confidentiality boundaries.
- As an administrator or governance user, I can understand the lifecycle and audit consequences of bylaw enforcement and compliance cases.
- As a collaborator, I receive deterministic errors and realtime/notification behavior when bylaw enforcement and compliance cases changes.

## 8. Functional Requirements
- **CASE-FR-001** — BylawCase SHALL belong to one Organization and MAY link complainant, subject party/Unit, Bylaw/Rule, Card and source IssueSubmission.
- **CASE-FR-002** — Case lifecycle SHALL support intake/review, investigation, notice, response, hearing where applicable, decision, enforcement, compliance and closure.
- **CASE-FR-003** — Evidence SHALL preserve uploader/source, timestamp, file/document relationship and integrity metadata.
- **CASE-FR-004** — Formal Notices SHALL use PRD-65 Correspondence and delivery tracking.
- **CASE-FR-005** — Hearing/Meeting relationships SHALL preserve Agenda/Minutes/Resolution decisions without copying them into the case.
- **CASE-FR-006** — Fine/enforcement action SHALL require explicit human/governance authorization and jurisdiction configuration; AI SHALL never impose it.
- **CASE-FR-007** — Case confidentiality SHALL default to restrictive Organization policy and SHALL not leak through search/dashboard/portal.
- **CASE-FR-008** — Case closure/reopening/appeal or reconsideration SHALL be auditable and preserve prior outcome.

## 9. Detailed Interaction Behaviour
- The UI SHALL load only records the user is authorized to know exist.
- Mutations SHALL optimistically update only when rollback/reconciliation is safe; the server remains authoritative.
- Concurrency-sensitive records SHALL use a revision/version precondition or equivalent stale-write protection.
- Shared changes SHALL be delivered through realtime/event infrastructure where another active user would reasonably expect immediate visibility.
- The interface SHALL preserve source/relationship context when navigating between related records.
- When a workflow requires human review, the UI SHALL make the pending human action and source evidence visible before approval.

## 10. Business Rules
- All records belong to one Organization unless a cross-Organization relationship is explicitly designed.
- Server-side authorization is authoritative; client controls are convenience only.
- Historical/audit records are not silently rewritten when current memberships or roles change.

## 11. Permission Rules
- VIEW requires Organization membership/portal access and object-level confidentiality as applicable.
- CREATE/EDIT/LINK require explicit domain permission; governance title alone is insufficient.
- DELETE/EXPORT/ADMINISTER require elevated permission and lifecycle/retention preconditions.
- SYSTEM/AI actor may perform only operations explicitly designated as automatable and must retain audit provenance.
- Every permission is enforced server-side. Portal authorization, where applicable, is evaluated independently from internal Board authorization.

## 12. Data Requirements
Primary entities: `BylawCase`, `EvidenceRecord`, `Bylaw`, `Correspondence`, `IssueSubmission`.

For every entity introduced or materially used by this PRD, PRD-20 SHALL define primary key, Organization ownership, foreign keys, cardinality, required/optional fields, indexes, unique constraints, lifecycle, versioning, archive/deletion/retention, confidentiality, authorization and audit behavior. Historical/governance entities must preserve referential meaning after user deactivation or operational record archive.

## 13. API Requirements
Representative operations: `POST /bylaw-cases`; `PATCH /bylaw-cases/{id}`; `POST /bylaw-cases/{id}/evidence`; `POST /bylaw-cases/{id}/close`.

All APIs SHALL schema-validate input, enforce Organization scope before disclosure, return stable error envelopes, use cursor pagination for unbounded collections, use idempotency keys for retry-prone side effects, and return authoritative revision/version on concurrency-sensitive mutations.

## 14. Real-Time / Event Requirements
Relevant domain events include: `BYLAW_CASE_CREATED`; `BYLAW_NOTICE_ISSUED`; `BYLAW_CASE_DECISION_RECORDED`; `BYLAW_CASE_CLOSED`.

Each event SHALL carry eventId, eventType, organizationId, authenticated actor/system actor, actingCapacity where relevant, entity type/ID, entity version where relevant, correlationId, safe metadata and createdAt. Subscribers receive only events they remain authorized to view.

## 15. UX Requirements
- Primary state, lifecycle, confidentiality and outstanding human action must be visually clear.
- Destructive or governance-significant actions require explicit confirmation and do not rely on color alone.
- Deep links preserve Organization context and return the user to the prior workflow where practical.
- Mobile web retains all critical review/approval/navigation operations even when layout is simplified.

## 16. Accessibility Requirements
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
- All controls require accessible names and visible keyboard focus.
- Dialog/drawer focus is trapped/restored correctly.
- Status, confidence, confidentiality and errors do not rely on color alone.
- Realtime updates use non-disruptive accessible announcements when they affect the current task.
- All critical review/approval/movement operations have keyboard equivalents.

## 17. Error and Empty States
- Empty state SHALL explain why no records exist and the next permitted action.
- Permission denial SHALL not leak protected titles, counts, snippets or identifiers.
- Validation errors SHALL identify actionable fields/rules.
- Network/integration failure SHALL preserve source/user work and expose retry or human fallback.
- Conflict SHALL explain that the record changed elsewhere and reload/merge authoritative state.
- Missing/deleted/merged/superseded records SHALL resolve to a lifecycle-aware state or safe not-found response.

## 18. Edge Cases
- User loses permission while record is open.
- Referenced parent/related entity becomes archived, merged, superseded or confidential.
- Duplicate network submission after client timeout.
- Concurrent edits produce version conflict.
- Realtime event arrives before mutation response or after reconnect.
- Organization/role/manager assignment changes during workflow.
- Record is subject to retention hold or approved-governance immutability.

## 19. Non-Functional Requirements
- All requests are Organization scoped and protected against cross-tenant ID enumeration.
- Mutation APIs use validation, stable errors and idempotency where retry is plausible.
- Sensitive content is excluded from application logs by default; correlation IDs remain available.
- Unbounded collections use cursor pagination and appropriate indexes.
- Relevant mutations emit domain events and authoritative AuditEvents.
- Primary synchronous mutation acknowledgement SHOULD target p95 <500 ms excluding external provider latency; long external/AI jobs run asynchronously with status.
- Security-relevant and governance-significant mutations SHALL remain recoverable/auditable across worker retries.

## 20. Analytics / Telemetry
- Feature adoption/use count by Organization without exposing sensitive content.
- Mutation success/error/permission-denial rate.
- p50/p95 latency for primary read/mutation operations.
- Conflict/retry/realtime recovery rate.
- User-visible failure and recovery rate.
- Analytics are not the source of truth for audit/governance history and SHALL avoid raw sensitive content unless explicitly justified.

## 21. Dependencies
- PRD-35
- PRD-50
- PRD-51
- PRD-65
- PRD-77

## 22. Out of Scope
Anything not explicitly required by this PRD or another referenced PRD.

**AC-CASE-64-03**  
GIVEN an authorized actor is operating within the correct Organization and lifecycle state

**AC-CASE-64-04**

15. Domain edge case: Duplicate network submission after client timeout.

definitions.body:
## Implementation ticket

### Adopted StrataAI2 architecture

- CI builds immutable web/API/Worker Docker images once and emits the tested images.

# PRD-66 — AGM / SGM Notice, Quorum, Proxies and General-Meeting Voting

## 1. PRD Identifier
**PRD-66**

## 2. Feature Name
**AGM / SGM Notice, Quorum, Proxies and General-Meeting Voting**

## 3. Executive Summary
Support owner/general-meeting governance separately from council-member voting.

## 4. Problem Statement
Strata operations combine ordinary work management with sensitive records, changing governance roles, formal decisions, external correspondence and long-lived history. Without explicit rules for **AGM / SGM Notice, Quorum, Proxies and General-Meeting Voting**, an implementation would be forced to invent lifecycle, data, permission and audit behavior, creating inconsistent or unsafe outcomes.

## 5. Product Objective
Deliver a production-ready implementation of **AGM / SGM Notice, Quorum, Proxies and General-Meeting Voting** that is Organization-scoped, permission-safe, auditable, accessible, and consistent with the canonical StrataAI model.

## 6. User Personas
- Organization Administrator — configures tenant-level policy and access.
- Council Member — performs governance and operational collaboration.
- President / Vice-President — performs council leadership tasks subject to explicit permissions.
- Strata Manager — acts professionally for assigned Organizations within delegated permissions.
- Property Management Company User — supports assigned manager/portfolio workflows.
- Owner / Resident — uses only the separated portal surface where invited.
- System / AI Service Actor — performs only explicitly authorized automated processing.

## 7. User Stories
- As an authorized user, I can use agm / sgm notice, quorum, proxies and general-meeting voting without bypassing Organization or confidentiality boundaries.
- As an administrator or governance user, I can understand the lifecycle and audit consequences of agm / sgm notice, quorum, proxies and general-meeting voting.
- As a collaborator, I receive deterministic errors and realtime/notification behavior when agm / sgm notice, quorum, proxies and general-meeting voting changes.

## 8. Functional Requirements
- **GMVOTE-FR-001** — General-meeting configuration SHALL support Notice, Agenda package, eligible voting interests/lots and quorum policy.
- **GMVOTE-FR-002** — VotingEntitlement SHALL represent who/what may vote and SHALL not assume one User equals one vote.
- **GMVOTE-FR-003** — Proxy SHALL link grantor/lot, proxy holder, meeting, scope, validation status and source Document where applicable.
- **GMVOTE-FR-004** — Proxy validation SHALL be explicit and auditable; invalid/expired/revoked proxy SHALL not count toward quorum/vote.
- **GMVOTE-FR-005** — Quorum SHALL be recalculable from eligible representation and attendance according to configurable jurisdiction policy.
- **GMVOTE-FR-006** — Ballot SHALL support resolution/motion, voting entitlement, vote value and secret-ballot mode where configured.
- **GMVOTE-FR-007** — Duplicate voting for the same entitlement SHALL be prevented or explicitly corrected through audited workflow.
- **GMVOTE-FR-008** — General-meeting vote thresholds/results SHALL preserve underlying counts/eligibility while avoiding disclosure prohibited by secret-ballot/privacy rules.

## 9. Detailed Interaction Behaviour
- The UI SHALL load only records the user is authorized to know exist.
- Mutations SHALL optimistically update only when rollback/reconciliation is safe; the server remains authoritative.
- Concurrency-sensitive records SHALL use a revision/version precondition or equivalent stale-write protection.
- Shared changes SHALL be delivered through realtime/event infrastructure where another active user would reasonably expect immediate visibility.
- The interface SHALL preserve source/relationship context when navigating between related records.
- When a workflow requires human review, the UI SHALL make the pending human action and source evidence visible before approval.

## 10. Business Rules
- All records belong to one Organization unless a cross-Organization relationship is explicitly designed.
- Server-side authorization is authoritative; client controls are convenience only.
- Historical/audit records are not silently rewritten when current memberships or roles change.

## 11. Permission Rules
- VIEW requires Organization membership/portal access and object-level confidentiality as applicable.
- CREATE/EDIT/LINK require explicit domain permission; governance title alone is insufficient.
- DELETE/EXPORT/ADMINISTER require elevated permission and lifecycle/retention preconditions.
- SYSTEM/AI actor may perform only operations explicitly designated as automatable and must retain audit provenance.
- Every permission is enforced server-side. Portal authorization, where applicable, is evaluated independently from internal Board authorization.

## 12. Data Requirements
Primary entities: `VotingEntitlement`, `Proxy`, `GeneralMeetingBallot`, `Meeting`, `Resolution`.

For every entity introduced or materially used by this PRD, PRD-20 SHALL define primary key, Organization ownership, foreign keys, cardinality, required/optional fields, indexes, unique constraints, lifecycle, versioning, archive/deletion/retention, confidentiality, authorization and audit behavior. Historical/governance entities must preserve referential meaning after user deactivation or operational record archive.

## 13. API Requirements
Representative operations: `POST /meetings/{id}/proxies`; `POST /meetings/{id}/ballots`; `GET /meetings/{id}/quorum`; `GET /meetings/{id}/general-vote-result`.

All APIs SHALL schema-validate input, enforce Organization scope before disclosure, return stable error envelopes, use cursor pagination for unbounded collections, use idempotency keys for retry-prone side effects, and return authoritative revision/version on concurrency-sensitive mutations.

## 14. Real-Time / Event Requirements
Relevant domain events include: `PROXY_RECORDED`; `PROXY_VALIDATED`; `GENERAL_MEETING_VOTE_RECORDED`; `GENERAL_MEETING_RESULT_CALCULATED`.

Each event SHALL carry eventId, eventType, organizationId, authenticated actor/system actor, actingCapacity where relevant, entity type/ID, entity version where relevant, correlationId, safe metadata and createdAt. Subscribers receive only events they remain authorized to view.

## 15. UX Requirements
- Primary state, lifecycle, confidentiality and outstanding human action must be visually clear.
- Destructive or governance-significant actions require explicit confirmation and do not rely on color alone.
- Deep links preserve Organization context and return the user to the prior workflow where practical.
- Mobile web retains all critical review/approval/navigation operations even when layout is simplified.

## 16. Accessibility Requirements
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
- All controls require accessible names and visible keyboard focus.
- Dialog/drawer focus is trapped/restored correctly.
- Status, confidence, confidentiality and errors do not rely on color alone.
- Realtime updates use non-disruptive accessible announcements when they affect the current task.
- All critical review/approval/movement operations have keyboard equivalents.

## 17. Error and Empty States
- Empty state SHALL explain why no records exist and the next permitted action.
- Permission denial SHALL not leak protected titles, counts, snippets or identifiers.
- Validation errors SHALL identify actionable fields/rules.
- Network/integration failure SHALL preserve source/user work and expose retry or human fallback.
- Conflict SHALL explain that the record changed elsewhere and reload/merge authoritative state.
- Missing/deleted/merged/superseded records SHALL resolve to a lifecycle-aware state or safe not-found response.

## 18. Edge Cases
- User loses permission while record is open.
- Referenced parent/related entity becomes archived, merged, superseded or confidential.
- Duplicate network submission after client timeout.
- Concurrent edits produce version conflict.
- Realtime event arrives before mutation response or after reconnect.
- Organization/role/manager assignment changes during workflow.
- Record is subject to retention hold or approved-governance immutability.

## 19. Non-Functional Requirements
- All requests are Organization scoped and protected against cross-tenant ID enumeration.
- Mutation APIs use validation, stable errors and idempotency where retry is plausible.
- Sensitive content is excluded from application logs by default; correlation IDs remain available.
- Unbounded collections use cursor pagination and appropriate indexes.
- Relevant mutations emit domain events and authoritative AuditEvents.
- Primary synchronous mutation acknowledgement SHOULD target p95 <500 ms excluding external provider latency; long external/AI jobs run asynchronously with status.
- Security-relevant and governance-significant mutations SHALL remain recoverable/auditable across worker retries.

## 20. Analytics / Telemetry
- Feature adoption/use count by Organization without exposing sensitive content.
- Mutation success/error/permission-denial rate.
- p50/p95 latency for primary read/mutation operations.
- Conflict/retry/realtime recovery rate.
- User-visible failure and recovery rate.
- Analytics are not the source of truth for audit/governance history and SHALL avoid raw sensitive content unless explicitly justified.

## 21. Dependencies
- PRD-37
- PRD-38
- PRD-42
- PRD-43
- PRD-70

## 22. Out of Scope
Anything not explicitly required by this PRD or another referenced PRD.

## 23. Acceptance Criteria
**AC-GMVOTE-66-01**  
GIVEN an authorized actor is operating within the correct Organization and lifecycle state  
WHEN the actor performs the behavior defined by **GMVOTE-FR-001**  
THEN the server validates authorization, confidentiality, version and business rules

# PRD-68 — Incident, Damage and Insurance Claim Management

## 1. PRD Identifier
**PRD-68**

## 2. Feature Name
**Incident, Damage and Insurance Claim Management**

## 3. Executive Summary
Track property incidents from initial event through emergency action, claim/remediation and closure.

## 4. Problem Statement
Strata operations combine ordinary work management with sensitive records, changing governance roles, formal decisions, external correspondence and long-lived history. Without explicit rules for **Incident, Damage and Insurance Claim Management**, an implementation would be forced to invent lifecycle, data, permission and audit behavior, creating inconsistent or unsafe outcomes.

## 5. Product Objective
Deliver a production-ready implementation of **Incident, Damage and Insurance Claim Management** that is Organization-scoped, permission-safe, auditable, accessible, and consistent with the canonical StrataAI model.

## 6. User Personas
- Organization Administrator — configures tenant-level policy and access.
- Council Member — performs governance and operational collaboration.
- President / Vice-President — performs council leadership tasks subject to explicit permissions.
- Strata Manager — acts professionally for assigned Organizations within delegated permissions.
- Property Management Company User — supports assigned manager/portfolio workflows.
- Owner / Resident — uses only the separated portal surface where invited.
- System / AI Service Actor — performs only explicitly authorized automated processing.

## 7. User Stories
- As an authorized user, I can use incident, damage and insurance claim management without bypassing Organization or confidentiality boundaries.
- As an administrator or governance user, I can understand the lifecycle and audit consequences of incident, damage and insurance claim management.
- As a collaborator, I receive deterministic errors and realtime/notification behavior when incident, damage and insurance claim management changes.

## 8. Functional Requirements
- **INCIDENT-FR-001** — Incident SHALL record type, occurred/discovered timestamps, description, severity, status, affected Lots/Assets/common property and reporter.
- **INCIDENT-FR-002** — Incident MAY create/link emergency Cards, Vendors, Documents/photos, Project and InsuranceClaim.
- **INCIDENT-FR-003** — InsuranceClaim SHALL store insurer/claim identifiers, adjuster/contact, dates, status, deductible/financial context and source Documents.
- **INCIDENT-FR-004** — Emergency actions SHALL be recorded with actor/time and SHALL not require a completed claim workflow before work can be tracked.
- **INCIDENT-FR-005** — Incident evidence SHALL preserve provenance and access controls.
- **INCIDENT-FR-006** — Incident status SHALL distinguish open response, claim pending, remediation, resolved/closed and cancelled/duplicate where needed.
- **INCIDENT-FR-007** — Closing Incident SHALL require outcome/remaining linked work acknowledgement.
- **INCIDENT-FR-008** — AI MAY classify/summarize incident correspondence but SHALL not make coverage/liability determinations.

## 9. Detailed Interaction Behaviour
- The UI SHALL load only records the user is authorized to know exist.
- Mutations SHALL optimistically update only when rollback/reconciliation is safe; the server remains authoritative.
- Concurrency-sensitive records SHALL use a revision/version precondition or equivalent stale-write protection.
- Shared changes SHALL be delivered through realtime/event infrastructure where another active user would reasonably expect immediate visibility.
- The interface SHALL preserve source/relationship context when navigating between related records.
- When a workflow requires human review, the UI SHALL make the pending human action and source evidence visible before approval.

## 10. Business Rules
- All records belong to one Organization unless a cross-Organization relationship is explicitly designed.
- Server-side authorization is authoritative; client controls are convenience only.
- Historical/audit records are not silently rewritten when current memberships or roles change.

## 11. Permission Rules
- VIEW requires Organization membership/portal access and object-level confidentiality as applicable.
- CREATE/EDIT/LINK require explicit domain permission; governance title alone is insufficient.
- DELETE/EXPORT/ADMINISTER require elevated permission and lifecycle/retention preconditions.
- SYSTEM/AI actor may perform only operations explicitly designated as automatable and must retain audit provenance.
- Every permission is enforced server-side. Portal authorization, where applicable, is evaluated independently from internal Board authorization.

## 12. Data Requirements
Primary entities: `Incident`, `InsuranceClaim`, `EvidenceRecord`, `Project`, `Card`.

For every entity introduced or materially used by this PRD, PRD-20 SHALL define primary key, Organization ownership, foreign keys, cardinality, required/optional fields, indexes, unique constraints, lifecycle, versioning, archive/deletion/retention, confidentiality, authorization and audit behavior. Historical/governance entities must preserve referential meaning after user deactivation or operational record archive.

## 13. API Requirements
Representative operations: `POST /incidents`; `POST /incidents/{id}/claims`; `PATCH /incidents/{id}`; `POST /incidents/{id}/close`.

All APIs SHALL schema-validate input, enforce Organization scope before disclosure, return stable error envelopes, use cursor pagination for unbounded collections, use idempotency keys for retry-prone side effects, and return authoritative revision/version on concurrency-sensitive mutations.

## 14. Real-Time / Event Requirements
Relevant domain events include: `INCIDENT_CREATED`; `EMERGENCY_ACTION_RECORDED`; `INSURANCE_CLAIM_CREATED`; `INCIDENT_CLOSED`.

Each event SHALL carry eventId, eventType, organizationId, authenticated actor/system actor, actingCapacity where relevant, entity type/ID, entity version where relevant, correlationId, safe metadata and createdAt. Subscribers receive only events they remain authorized to view.

## 15. UX Requirements
- Primary state, lifecycle, confidentiality and outstanding human action must be visually clear.
- Destructive or governance-significant actions require explicit confirmation and do not rely on color alone.
- Deep links preserve Organization context and return the user to the prior workflow where practical.
- Mobile web retains all critical review/approval/navigation operations even when layout is simplified.

## 16. Accessibility Requirements
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
- All controls require accessible names and visible keyboard focus.
- Dialog/drawer focus is trapped/restored correctly.
- Status, confidence, confidentiality and errors do not rely on color alone.
- Realtime updates use non-disruptive accessible announcements when they affect the current task.
- All critical review/approval/movement operations have keyboard equivalents.

## 17. Error and Empty States
- Empty state SHALL explain why no records exist and the next permitted action.
- Permission denial SHALL not leak protected titles, counts, snippets or identifiers.
- Validation errors SHALL identify actionable fields/rules.
- Network/integration failure SHALL preserve source/user work and expose retry or human fallback.
- Conflict SHALL explain that the record changed elsewhere and reload/merge authoritative state.
- Missing/deleted/merged/superseded records SHALL resolve to a lifecycle-aware state or safe not-found response.

## 18. Edge Cases
- User loses permission while record is open.
- Referenced parent/related entity becomes archived, merged, superseded or confidential.
- Duplicate network submission after client timeout.
- Concurrent edits produce version conflict.
- Realtime event arrives before mutation response or after reconnect.
- Organization/role/manager assignment changes during workflow.
- Record is subject to retention hold or approved-governance immutability.

## 19. Non-Functional Requirements
- All requests are Organization scoped and protected against cross-tenant ID enumeration.
- Mutation APIs use validation, stable errors and idempotency where retry is plausible.
- Sensitive content is excluded from application logs by default; correlation IDs remain available.
- Unbounded collections use cursor pagination and appropriate indexes.
- Relevant mutations emit domain events and authoritative AuditEvents.
- Primary synchronous mutation acknowledgement SHOULD target p95 <500 ms excluding external provider latency; long external/AI jobs run asynchronously with status.
- Security-relevant and governance-significant mutations SHALL remain recoverable/auditable across worker retries.

## 20. Analytics / Telemetry
- Feature adoption/use count by Organization without exposing sensitive content.
- Mutation success/error/permission-denial rate.
- p50/p95 latency for primary read/mutation operations.
- Conflict/retry/realtime recovery rate.
- User-visible failure and recovery rate.
- Analytics are not the source of truth for audit/governance history and SHALL avoid raw sensitive content unless explicitly justified.

## 21. Dependencies
- PRD-28
- PRD-34
- PRD-36
- PRD-45
- PRD-69

## 22. Out of Scope
Anything not explicitly required by this PRD or another referenced PRD.

GIVEN an authorized actor is operating within the correct Organization and lifecycle state  
WHEN the actor performs the behavior defined by **INCIDENT-FR-001**  
THEN the server validates authorization, confidentiality, version and business rules  
AND the authoritative state is persisted or the operation is rejected atomically  
AND required Activity/Audit/domain events are produced without leaking protected information.

1. Primary happy path and persisted refresh behavior.
2. Empty/no-data state and first permitted action.

# PRD-70 — Records Retention, Privacy, Redaction, Legal Hold and Data Export

## 1. PRD Identifier
**PRD-70**

## 2. Feature Name
**Records Retention, Privacy, Redaction, Legal Hold and Data Export**

## 3. Executive Summary
Apply explicit record-class lifecycle/retention policy to operational, governance, audit, correspondence, documents and AI records.

## 4. Problem Statement
Strata operations combine ordinary work management with sensitive records, changing governance roles, formal decisions, external correspondence and long-lived history. Without explicit rules for **Records Retention, Privacy, Redaction, Legal Hold and Data Export**, an implementation would be forced to invent lifecycle, data, permission and audit behavior, creating inconsistent or unsafe outcomes.

## 5. Product Objective
Deliver a production-ready implementation of **Records Retention, Privacy, Redaction, Legal Hold and Data Export** that is Organization-scoped, permission-safe, auditable, accessible, and consistent with the canonical StrataAI model.

## 6. User Personas
- Organization Administrator — configures tenant-level policy and access.
- Council Member — performs governance and operational collaboration.
- President / Vice-President — performs council leadership tasks subject to explicit permissions.
- Strata Manager — acts professionally for assigned Organizations within delegated permissions.
- Property Management Company User — supports assigned manager/portfolio workflows.
- Owner / Resident — uses only the separated portal surface where invited.
- System / AI Service Actor — performs only explicitly authorized automated processing.

## 7. User Stories
- As an authorized user, I can use records retention, privacy, redaction, legal hold and data export without bypassing Organization or confidentiality boundaries.
- As an administrator or governance user, I can understand the lifecycle and audit consequences of records retention, privacy, redaction, legal hold and data export.
- As a collaborator, I receive deterministic errors and realtime/notification behavior when records retention, privacy, redaction, legal hold and data export changes.

## 8. Functional Requirements
- **RECORDS-FR-001** — RecordRetentionPolicy SHALL identify record class/category, retention rule, disposition action and jurisdiction/Organization applicability.
- **RECORDS-FR-002** — Governance records SHALL not inherit generic Card permanent-deletion semantics.
- **RECORDS-FR-003** — Legal/RetentionHold SHALL suspend ordinary disposition for in-scope records and SHALL be audited.
- **RECORDS-FR-004** — Redaction SHALL create a controlled derived/display form while preserving authorized access to original where policy requires.
- **RECORDS-FR-005** — Export SHALL enforce authorization, scope, confidentiality and audit; large exports SHALL use expiring secure downloads.
- **RECORDS-FR-006** — Data-subject/privacy actions SHALL distinguish deletion/anonymization requirements from governance/audit retention obligations.
- **RECORDS-FR-007** — Disposition jobs SHALL be idempotent, auditable and recoverable from failure.
- **RECORDS-FR-008** — Organization offboarding SHALL produce documented export/retention/deletion steps and verification.

## 9. Detailed Interaction Behaviour
- The UI SHALL load only records the user is authorized to know exist.
- Mutations SHALL optimistically update only when rollback/reconciliation is safe; the server remains authoritative.
- Concurrency-sensitive records SHALL use a revision/version precondition or equivalent stale-write protection.
- Shared changes SHALL be delivered through realtime/event infrastructure where another active user would reasonably expect immediate visibility.
- The interface SHALL preserve source/relationship context when navigating between related records.
- When a workflow requires human review, the UI SHALL make the pending human action and source evidence visible before approval.

## 10. Business Rules
- All records belong to one Organization unless a cross-Organization relationship is explicitly designed.
- Server-side authorization is authoritative; client controls are convenience only.
- Historical/audit records are not silently rewritten when current memberships or roles change.

## 11. Permission Rules
- VIEW requires Organization membership/portal access and object-level confidentiality as applicable.
- CREATE/EDIT/LINK require explicit domain permission; governance title alone is insufficient.
- DELETE/EXPORT/ADMINISTER require elevated permission and lifecycle/retention preconditions.
- SYSTEM/AI actor may perform only operations explicitly designated as automatable and must retain audit provenance.
- Every permission is enforced server-side. Portal authorization, where applicable, is evaluated independently from internal Board authorization.

## 12. Data Requirements
Primary entities: `RecordRetentionPolicy`, `RetentionHold`, `Redaction`, `ExportJob`.

For every entity introduced or materially used by this PRD, PRD-20 SHALL define primary key, Organization ownership, foreign keys, cardinality, required/optional fields, indexes, unique constraints, lifecycle, versioning, archive/deletion/retention, confidentiality, authorization and audit behavior. Historical/governance entities must preserve referential meaning after user deactivation or operational record archive.

## 13. API Requirements
Representative operations: `GET/PATCH /retention-policies`; `POST /retention-holds`; `POST /records/export`; `POST /records/disposition`.

All APIs SHALL schema-validate input, enforce Organization scope before disclosure, return stable error envelopes, use cursor pagination for unbounded collections, use idempotency keys for retry-prone side effects, and return authoritative revision/version on concurrency-sensitive mutations.

## 14. Real-Time / Event Requirements
Relevant domain events include: `RETENTION_HOLD_APPLIED`; `RECORD_REDACTED`; `EXPORT_CREATED`; `RECORD_DISPOSED`.

Each event SHALL carry eventId, eventType, organizationId, authenticated actor/system actor, actingCapacity where relevant, entity type/ID, entity version where relevant, correlationId, safe metadata and createdAt. Subscribers receive only events they remain authorized to view.

## 15. UX Requirements
- Primary state, lifecycle, confidentiality and outstanding human action must be visually clear.
- Destructive or governance-significant actions require explicit confirmation and do not rely on color alone.
- Deep links preserve Organization context and return the user to the prior workflow where practical.
- Mobile web retains all critical review/approval/navigation operations even when layout is simplified.

## 16. Accessibility Requirements
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
- All controls require accessible names and visible keyboard focus.
- Dialog/drawer focus is trapped/restored correctly.
- Status, confidence, confidentiality and errors do not rely on color alone.
- Realtime updates use non-disruptive accessible announcements when they affect the current task.
- All critical review/approval/movement operations have keyboard equivalents.

## 17. Error and Empty States
- Empty state SHALL explain why no records exist and the next permitted action.
- Permission denial SHALL not leak protected titles, counts, snippets or identifiers.
- Validation errors SHALL identify actionable fields/rules.
- Network/integration failure SHALL preserve source/user work and expose retry or human fallback.
- Conflict SHALL explain that the record changed elsewhere and reload/merge authoritative state.
- Missing/deleted/merged/superseded records SHALL resolve to a lifecycle-aware state or safe not-found response.

## 18. Edge Cases
- User loses permission while record is open.
- Referenced parent/related entity becomes archived, merged, superseded or confidential.
- Duplicate network submission after client timeout.
- Concurrent edits produce version conflict.
- Realtime event arrives before mutation response or after reconnect.
- Organization/role/manager assignment changes during workflow.
- Record is subject to retention hold or approved-governance immutability.

## 19. Non-Functional Requirements
- All requests are Organization scoped and protected against cross-tenant ID enumeration.
- Mutation APIs use validation, stable errors and idempotency where retry is plausible.
- Sensitive content is excluded from application logs by default; correlation IDs remain available.
- Unbounded collections use cursor pagination and appropriate indexes.
- Relevant mutations emit domain events and authoritative AuditEvents.
- Primary synchronous mutation acknowledgement SHOULD target p95 <500 ms excluding external provider latency; long external/AI jobs run asynchronously with status.
- Security-relevant and governance-significant mutations SHALL remain recoverable/auditable across worker retries.

- p50/p95 latency for primary read/mutation operations.
- Conflict/retry/realtime recovery rate.
- User-visible failure and recovery rate.
- Analytics are not the source of truth for audit/governance history and SHALL avoid raw sensitive content unless explicitly justified.

- PRD-48
- PRD-53
- PRD-59

## 22. Out of Scope
Anything not explicitly required by this PRD or another referenced PRD.

GIVEN an authorized actor is operating within the correct Organization and lifecycle state

- **AI-FR-005** — AI SHALL support confidence/uncertainty handling and route low-confidence results to human review.
- **AI-FR-006** — Externally supplied content SHALL be treated as untrusted data; prompt-injection content SHALL not override system/application policy.

- SYSTEM/AI actor may perform only operations explicitly designated as automatable and must retain audit provenance.

## 13. API Requirements

## 14. Real-Time / Event Requirements

## 15. UX Requirements
- Primary state, lifecycle, confidentiality and outstanding human action must be visually clear.

- Validation errors SHALL identify actionable fields/rules.
- Network/integration failure SHALL preserve source/user work and expose retry or human fallback.
- Conflict SHALL explain that the record changed elsewhere and reload/merge authoritative state.
- Missing/deleted/merged/superseded records SHALL resolve to a lifecycle-aware state or safe not-found response.

- User loses permission while record is open.
- Referenced parent/related entity becomes archived, merged, superseded or confidential.
- Duplicate network submission after client timeout.
- Concurrent edits produce version conflict.

- SYSTEM/AI actor may perform only operations explicitly designated as automatable and must retain audit provenance.
- Every permission is enforced server-side. Portal authorization, where applicable, is evaluated independently from internal Board authorization.

Each event SHALL carry eventId, eventType, organizationId, authenticated actor/system actor, actingCapacity where relevant, entity type/ID, entity version where relevant, correlationId, safe metadata and createdAt. Subscribers receive only events they remain authorized to view.

## 15. UX Requirements
- Primary state, lifecycle, confidentiality and outstanding human action must be visually clear.
- Destructive or governance-significant actions require explicit confirmation and do not rely on color alone.
- Deep links preserve Organization context and return the user to the prior workflow where practical.
- Mobile web retains all critical review/approval/navigation operations even when layout is simplified.

- Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
- All controls require accessible names and visible keyboard focus.
- Dialog/drawer focus is trapped/restored correctly.
- Status, confidence, confidentiality and errors do not rely on color alone.
- Realtime updates use non-disruptive accessible announcements when they affect the current task.
- All critical review/approval/movement operations have keyboard equivalents.

## 17. Error and Empty States

- Permission denial SHALL not leak protected titles, counts, snippets or identifiers.
- Validation errors SHALL identify actionable fields/rules.
- Network/integration failure SHALL preserve source/user work and expose retry or human fallback.
- Conflict SHALL explain that the record changed elsewhere and reload/merge authoritative state.
- Missing/deleted/merged/superseded records SHALL resolve to a lifecycle-aware state or safe not-found response.

- Referenced parent/related entity becomes archived, merged, superseded or confidential.
- Duplicate network submission after client timeout.
- Concurrent edits produce version conflict.
- Realtime event arrives before mutation response or after reconnect.
- Organization/role/manager assignment changes during workflow.
- Record is subject to retention hold or approved-governance immutability.

- System / AI Service Actor — performs only explicitly authorized automated processing.

## 7. User Stories

- **MAIL-FR-008** — Outbound sending SHALL use idempotency/duplicate-send protection and safe retry after ambiguous network failure.
- **MAIL-FR-009** — Bounce/provider delivery failures SHALL be recorded/notified where available; repeated automatic retry spam is prohibited.
- **MAIL-FR-010** — Mailbox disconnection SHALL preserve records, block send, flag sync health and notify authorized admins/managers.

# PRD-80 — Owner and Resident Portal

## 1. PRD Identifier
**PRD-80**

## 2. Feature Name
**Owner and Resident Portal**

## 3. Executive Summary
Provide an invitation-only, security-isolated owner/resident portal with a simple folder-based document library and optional issue intake.

## 4. Problem Statement
Strata operations combine ordinary work management with sensitive records, changing governance roles, formal decisions, external correspondence and long-lived history. Without explicit rules for **Owner and Resident Portal**, an implementation would be forced to invent lifecycle, data, permission and audit behavior, creating inconsistent or unsafe outcomes.

## 5. Product Objective
Deliver a production-ready implementation of **Owner and Resident Portal** that is Organization-scoped, permission-safe, auditable, accessible, and consistent with the canonical StrataAI model.

## 6. User Personas
- Owner / Resident Portal User — views only explicitly published resources and their permitted issue status.
- Council Member — may invite portal users and manage portal content subject to internal permissions.
- Strata Manager — may invite/manage portal content for assigned Organizations.
- Organization Administrator — configures portal policy without making portal users internal Board members.

## 7. User Stories
- As an authorized user, I can use owner and resident portal without bypassing Organization or confidentiality boundaries.
- As an administrator or governance user, I can understand the lifecycle and audit consequences of owner and resident portal.
- As a collaborator, I receive deterministic errors and realtime/notification behavior when owner and resident portal changes.

## 8. Functional Requirements
- **PORTAL-FR-001** — Portal SHALL be a separate authorization surface; PortalAccess SHALL never imply OrganizationMember, BoardMember or internal Card access.
- **PORTAL-FR-002** — Any current Council Member or assigned Strata Manager MAY invite an owner/resident subject to Organization policy; invitation authority SHALL not broaden the inviter's own internal permissions.
- **PORTAL-FR-003** — Portal invitations SHALL use secure single-use expiring revocable tokens bound to Organization and invited email and SHALL reuse existing User identity when present.
- **PORTAL-FR-004** — PortalAccess lifecycle SHALL support INVITED, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, REVOKED and EXPIRED and MAY link one or more authorized StrataLot relationships.
- **PORTAL-FR-005** — Portal home SHALL expose Organization/property info, associated Units, published Documents, configured contacts, issue submission/status and notifications only.
- **PORTAL-FR-006** — PortalFolder SHALL support parent/child hierarchy, name/description/rank/visibility/lifecycle and authorized Council/Manager management.
- **PORTAL-FR-007** — PortalDocumentPublication SHALL explicitly publish an existing Document into a PortalFolder with display title, publication/effective/expiry dates, visibility scope and DRAFT/PUBLISHED/UNPUBLISHED/ARCHIVED state.
- **PORTAL-FR-008** — Internal Document relationships SHALL never imply portal publication; unpublished/draft/confidential Documents SHALL remain hidden.
- **PORTAL-FR-009** — Publication visibility SHALL support ALL_PORTAL_USERS, SPECIFIC_UNITS, SPECIFIC_USERS, OWNERS_ONLY, RESIDENTS_ONLY and extensible groups.
- **PORTAL-FR-010** — Portal users SHALL browse/open/download permitted Documents but SHALL not edit authoritative Documents or see internal comments/relationships.
- **PORTAL-FR-011** — Portal search SHALL index only portal-visible folders/Documents and SHALL never leak internal titles, counts, snippets or hidden records.
- **PORTAL-FR-012** — Issue intake SHALL map internal workflow to simplified portal statuses RECEIVED, UNDER_REVIEW, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_INFORMATION, RESOLVED and CLOSED.
- **PORTAL-FR-013** — Portal notifications SHALL cover invitations, document publications/updates, issue acknowledgement/status and intended correspondence without confidential previews.
- **PORTAL-FR-014** — All portal APIs/downloads/signed URLs SHALL enforce portal-specific server-side authorization independently of internal Board authorization.
- **PORTAL-FR-015** — Portal security testing SHALL include horizontal owner access, cross-Organization access, unit restrictions, expired/revoked invitation/access, direct URL/signed URL abuse, folder enumeration and search leakage.

## 9. Detailed Interaction Behaviour
- The UI SHALL load only records the user is authorized to know exist.
- Mutations SHALL optimistically update only when rollback/reconciliation is safe; the server remains authoritative.
- Concurrency-sensitive records SHALL use a revision/version precondition or equivalent stale-write protection.
- Shared changes SHALL be delivered through realtime/event infrastructure where another active user would reasonably expect immediate visibility.
- The interface SHALL preserve source/relationship context when navigating between related records.
- When a workflow requires human review, the UI SHALL make the pending human action and source evidence visible before approval.

## 10. Business Rules
- Portal users are NOT Board Members merely because they have portal access.
- Publishing is explicit: DocumentRelationship does not equal PortalDocumentPublication.
- Owner/Resident issue submission may create/link internal Cards, but internal Card state/comments remain hidden unless deliberately mapped to portal-facing fields.

## 11. Permission Rules
- VIEW requires Organization membership/portal access and object-level confidentiality as applicable.
- CREATE/EDIT/LINK require explicit domain permission; governance title alone is insufficient.
- DELETE/EXPORT/ADMINISTER require elevated permission and lifecycle/retention preconditions.
- SYSTEM/AI actor may perform only operations explicitly designated as automatable and must retain audit provenance.
- Every permission is enforced server-side. Portal authorization, where applicable, is evaluated independently from internal Board authorization.

## 12. Data Requirements
Primary entities: `PortalAccess`, `PortalInvitation`, `PortalFolder`, `PortalDocumentPublication`, `PortalNotificationPreference`, `Document`, `IssueSubmission`.

For every entity introduced or materially used by this PRD, PRD-20 SHALL define primary key, Organization ownership, foreign keys, cardinality, required/optional fields, indexes, unique constraints, lifecycle, versioning, archive/deletion/retention, confidentiality, authorization and audit behavior. Historical/governance entities must preserve referential meaning after user deactivation or operational record archive.

## 13. API Requirements
Representative operations: `POST /portal/invitations`; `POST /portal/invitations/{token}/accept`; `GET /portal/folders`; `POST /portal/folders`; `POST /portal/publications`; `GET /portal/documents/{id}`; `POST /portal/issues`.

All APIs SHALL schema-validate input, enforce Organization scope before disclosure, return stable error envelopes, use cursor pagination for unbounded collections, use idempotency keys for retry-prone side effects, and return authoritative revision/version on concurrency-sensitive mutations.

## 14. Real-Time / Event Requirements
Relevant domain events include: `PORTAL_INVITATION_CREATED`; `PORTAL_INVITATION_ACCEPTED`; `PORTAL_ACCESS_REVOKED`; `PORTAL_FOLDER_CREATED`; `PORTAL_DOCUMENT_PUBLISHED`; `PORTAL_DOCUMENT_UNPUBLISHED`; `PORTAL_DOCUMENT_DOWNLOADED`; `ISSUE_SUBMITTED_BY_PORTAL_USER`.

Each event SHALL carry eventId, eventType, organizationId, authenticated actor/system actor, actingCapacity where relevant, entity type/ID, entity version where relevant, correlationId, safe metadata and createdAt. Subscribers receive only events they remain authorized to view.

## 15. UX Requirements
- Primary state, lifecycle, confidentiality and outstanding human action must be visually clear.
- Destructive or governance-significant actions require explicit confirmation and do not rely on color alone.
- Deep links preserve Organization context and return the user to the prior workflow where practical.
- Mobile web retains all critical review/approval/navigation operations even when layout is simplified.

## 16. Accessibility Requirements
- Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
- All controls require accessible names and visible keyboard focus.
- Dialog/drawer focus is trapped/restored correctly.
- Status, confidence, confidentiality and errors do not rely on color alone.
- Realtime updates use non-disruptive accessible announcements when they affect the current task.
- All critical review/approval/movement operations have keyboard equivalents.

## 17. Error and Empty States
- Empty state SHALL explain why no records exist and the next permitted action.
- Permission denial SHALL not leak protected titles, counts, snippets or identifiers.
- Validation errors SHALL identify actionable fields/rules.
- Network/integration failure SHALL preserve source/user work and expose retry or human fallback.
- Conflict SHALL explain that the record changed elsewhere and reload/merge authoritative state.
- Missing/deleted/merged/superseded records SHALL resolve to a lifecycle-aware state or safe not-found response.

## 18. Edge Cases
- User loses permission while record is open.
- Referenced parent/related entity becomes archived, merged, superseded or confidential.
- Duplicate network submission after client timeout.
- Concurrent edits produce version conflict.
- Realtime event arrives before mutation response or after reconnect.
- Organization/role/manager assignment changes during workflow.
- Record is subject to retention hold or approved-governance immutability.

## 19. Non-Functional Requirements
- All requests are Organization scoped and protected against cross-tenant ID enumeration.
- Mutation APIs use validation, stable errors and idempotency where retry is plausible.
- Sensitive content is excluded from application logs by default; correlation IDs remain available.
- Unbounded collections use cursor pagination and appropriate indexes.
- Relevant mutations emit domain events and authoritative AuditEvents.
- Primary synchronous mutation acknowledgement SHOULD target p95 <500 ms excluding external provider latency; long external/AI jobs run asynchronously with status.
- Security-relevant and governance-significant mutations SHALL remain recoverable/auditable across worker retries.

## 20. Analytics / Telemetry
- Feature adoption/use count by Organization without exposing sensitive content.
- Mutation success/error/permission-denial rate.
- p50/p95 latency for primary read/mutation operations.
- Conflict/retry/realtime recovery rate.
- User-visible failure and recovery rate.
- Analytics are not the source of truth for audit/governance history and SHALL avoid raw sensitive content unless explicitly justified.

---

# Recommended Vertical-Slice Implementation Sequence

## Slice 1 — Foundation
Authentication → Organization → membership → Board → List → basic Card.

## Slice 2 — Core Kanban
Card/List movement → persistent ordering → Card detail → realtime synchronization.

## Slice 3 — Card Capabilities
Descriptions → Labels → Members → dates → Checklists → Attachments → Comments → Activity.

## Slice 4 — Strata Foundation
Organization configuration → Lots → Party/Lot history → Council terms/roles → Manager/Management Company.

## Slice 5 — Strata Card Model
Priority/category/source → affected Lots/common property → confidentiality → relationships.

## Slice 6 — Property Operations
Property/buildings/common areas/assets → recurring maintenance → inspections/service history.

## Slice 7 — Meeting Governance
Meetings → attendance → notices/distribution → Agendas → Minutes → approval.

## Slice 8 — Decision Management
Motions → council Votes → Resolutions → follow-up Cards.

## Slice 9 — Approval Infrastructure
ApprovalRequest → reviewer eligibility → version-safe decisions → notifications/audit.

## Slice 10 — Project/Vendor/Financial Context
Projects → Vendors → Quotes → Contracts/Invoices → FinancialAuthorization.

## Slice 11 — Documents and Bylaws
Documents → versioning/relationships → Bylaws/Rules → retention metadata.

## Slice 12 — Owner/Resident Workflows
Issue intake → Card routing → BylawCase when applicable → Correspondence → outcome.

## Slice 13 — Incidents and Insurance
Incident → emergency work/evidence → InsuranceClaim → remediation Project → closeout.

## Slice 14 — Card Reconciliation
Duplicate detection → merge preview → merge/redirect → split → correction feedback.

## Slice 15 — First AI Production Workflow
Shared inbound mailbox → email ingest/threading → AI triage → Card match/create → context summary → next-action recommendation → response draft → human review.

## Slice 16 — Email Round Trip
Approval → outbound send → delivery/bounce → reply threading → same Card Correspondence timeline.

## Slice 17 — Owner Portal
Portal invitation → Unit relationship → separate PortalAccess → folders → explicit Document publication → owner download/search → issue intake.

## Slice 18 — Search, Dashboard, Reporting and Calendar
Global search → related records → dashboards → reporting → calendar/deadlines.

## Slice 19 — AI Assistants
Permission-aware Q&A → Document intelligence → Meeting/Agenda/Minutes assistant.

## Slice 20 — Records Governance and Hardening
Retention/legal hold/redaction/export → backup/restore → security → accessibility → performance → concurrency → E2E and load testing.

Each slice must define migrations, APIs, events, UI, authorization, tests, observability, migration concerns and measurable completion criteria before implementation begins.

---

# Cross-PRD Consistency Review

- **Tenant:** Organization is canonical everywhere; Organization is not a separate entity.
- **Internal vs portal:** PortalAccess is separate from OrganizationMember/BoardMember.
- **Roles:** Authentication, application permission, membership, governance role, professional role, unit relationship and acting capacity are separate.
- **Lifecycle:** Operational deletion rules do not apply to immutable governance/audit records.
- **Confidentiality:** The most restrictive applicable policy wins; search/count/notification/realtime/AI/portal leakage is prohibited.
- **AI:** Human-in-the-loop boundaries are consistent; official outbound correspondence is never sent solely by AI.
- **Email:** Inbound original evidence, AI draft, human edit, approved version and sent version remain distinct.
- **Merges:** Merged Card IDs remain resolvable; historical links/audit are preserved.
- **Meetings:** Council voting and general-meeting entitlement/proxy voting are distinct.
- **Documents:** Internal relationship is not portal publication; authoritative versions are preserved.
- **Retention:** Legal hold overrides ordinary disposition; governance history is not silently deleted.
- **Realtime:** All realtime/event delivery is authorization-filtered at subscription and event-dispatch time.
- **Jurisdiction:** The product models configurable mechanisms and does not invent legal requirements.

---

# Product-Level Success Measures

Measure at least: inbound email triage success; existing-Card match precision; duplicate Card creation rate; AI recommendation accept/edit/reject distribution; draft-response acceptance/edit rate; median email-to-triage time; median issue-to-assignment time; overdue Card rate; unresolved meeting follow-up rate; Resolutions with tracked follow-up; agenda/minutes preparation time; search success; AI grounding/citation coverage; portal document-access success; system availability; provider failure rate; permission-denial anomalies; backup restore-test success. Metrics must never encourage unsafe automation or weaken human review.

---

# Final Quality Gate

The suite is ready for implementation only when every PRD and cross-cutting architecture can answer: who can see/change the record; tenant ownership; internal vs portal surface; historical role context; physical Unit/Asset context; archive/delete/immutability/retention behavior; emitted domain/audit events; concurrency behavior; integration failure behavior; empty/error/mobile/keyboard behavior; search/notification/AI leakage prevention; AI context and approval boundary; correction/audit of AI mistakes; duplicate reconciliation; inbound-to-outbound email provenance; portal invitation/publication security; and end-to-end traceability from original source through final decision and completion.

---

## Linked test cases
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-01** — Primary happy path and persisted refresh behavior.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-02** — Empty/no-data state and first permitted action.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-03** — Invalid input and schema/business-rule failure.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-04** — Unauthorized user and confidentiality-protected target.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-05** — Cross-Organization ID substitution attempt.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-06** — User loses permission mid-session.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-07** — Network timeout, safe retry and idempotency where applicable.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-08** — Concurrent stale-version update.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-09** — Realtime disconnect/reconnect and missed-event recovery.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-10** — Archive/supersede/retention-hold interaction.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-11** — Keyboard-only and screen-reader critical flow.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-12** — Mobile web critical flow.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-13** — Domain edge case: User loses permission while record is open.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-14** — Domain edge case: Referenced parent/related entity becomes archived, merged, superseded or confidential.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-15** — Domain edge case: Duplicate network submission after client timeout.
- [ ] **PRD-80-TC-16** — Domain edge case: Concurrent edits produce version conflict.

## Agent execution contract
- Implement all PRD requirements and acceptance criteria; do not silently narrow scope.
- Preserve Organization/tenant isolation and the separate Owner Portal authorization surface.
- Add/update automated tests before closure and reference PRD/AC/test IDs.
- Include migrations, authorization, events, audit, accessibility, concurrency, errors/empty states, and observability where required.
- Link the implementation pull request to this issue and include executed test evidence.
- Do not add a datastore, broker, framework, or deployable service without an approved architecture decision.

# UX-001: Application Shell and Responsive Navigation

Status: Slice 1 implemented locally; validation recorded in delivery report. Full UX-001 remains unaccepted: global account pages, human review, real-service regression and release checks remain.

Incremental UX delivery workstream. Canonical business/security requirements remain in PRD-01 FOUND-FR-005–008; ARCH-02; PRD-23; PRD-80. ## Dependencies

Existing InternalAppShell, React Router, SurfaceAdmission, MUI Drawer and appTheme. UX-002/003 refine this increment; they do not block an additive shell fix.

## User journeys

Internal member opens a stable Board/Card deep link, identifies context, opens navigation on a phone, visits Notifications, then returns with browser Back. Keyboard user skips repeated navigation. Portal-only user cannot mount internal navigation.

## Implementation tasks

- [x] UX-001-T-01: Inventory current routes, landmarks, breakpoint behavior and protected recovery exceptions before changing composition.
- [x] UX-001-T-02: Use one destination definition for desktop and temporary mobile MUI drawers; retain stable URLs, NavigationConfirmation and protected Outlet ownership.

## Acceptance criteria

- UX-001-AC-01: Existing Board/Card deep links and browser Back preserve context; no API, schema, tenant or original-command recovery behavior changes.
- UX-001-AC-02: At widths below 600px, keyboard/touch users can open/close the shared drawer, choose Organizations/Boards/Notifications and return focus after dismissal. Unimplemented modules remain disabled; no new routes.

## Automated tests

Phone user completes a Card action without page overflow; keyboard user moves a Card without dragging; zoom/screen-reader user follows dialogs, errors and realtime updates.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] UX-006-T-01: Inventory actual screens at 320/390/768/1280px and 200% text zoom / equivalent 400% reflow; prioritize operational MVP blockers.
- [ ] UX-006-T-02: Repair wrapping/overflow and touch targets incrementally; retain intentional local Kanban scrolling.
- [ ] UX-006-T-03: Audit landmarks/headings/labels, visible focus, contrast, keyboard drag alternatives and bounded live announcements.
- [ ] UX-006-T-04: Record automated results and manual assistive-technology/physical-device review separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- UX-006-AC-01: Critical MVP workflows remain available at every supported width without page-level horizontal scroll, clipped controls or lost data.
- UX-006-AC-02: WCAG 2.2 AA checks cover keyboard, focus visibility/not obscured, names, contrast and minimum target sizing under PRD-23.
- UX-006-AC-03: Pointer operations have keyboard equivalents; dialogs and realtime events maintain predictable focus and announcements.
- UX-006-AC-04: Axe pass is necessary evidence, not full accessibility acceptance; manual review and exceptions are recorded.

## Automated tests

- UX-006-TC-01: Unit: state semantics, focus and keyboard alternatives for changed components.
- UX-006-TC-02: Playwright: viewport fit, text zoom/reflow, touch and keyboard complete workflows with Axe at four widths.
- UX-006-TC-03: Regression: existing Kanban keyboard/touch, lifecycle/recovery and Portal tests; human screen-reader and physical-device acceptance logged separately.

## Delivery and acceptance

Use the [shared feature UX acceptance addendum](feature-acceptance.md) and [single delivery report](delivery-report.md). Record implemented, tested and accepted separately. Tests above are required coverage, not a claim of execution. Existing feature delivery can proceed where it does not mutate shared shell/navigation/theme files. One owner edits those files in each integration window; feature owners consume approved slots. Use a small PR per migration; use a reversible feature flag before any migration that would interrupt an existing workflow. This additive specification does not flag or replace working business functionality.

Acceptance requires all applicable quality gates, current revision evidence, documented failure evaluation and role-specific end-to-end review. UX completion cannot raise functional completion or MVP readiness by itself.

# UX-008: UX Regression Testing and Visual Validation

Status: Specified; first shell interaction coverage added, visual baselines and release acceptance pending.

## Scope and ownership

## Dependencies

UX-001/003 representative fixtures; UX-006 accessibility matrix. Extend existing Vitest, Playwright/Axe and immutable build-once CI.

## User journeys

Developer changes a shared token or navigation item; CI identifies affected workflows; reviewer compares approved visuals; failed check is evaluated before merge.

## Implementation tasks

- [ ] UX-008-T-01: Create stable route/state/role/viewport coverage map; keep controlled fixtures distinct from real API integration.
- [ ] UX-008-T-02: Register new cases in existing browser collection/sharding; add deterministic visual fixtures without overwriting approved baselines automatically.
- [ ] UX-008-T-03: Pin browser/runtime/fonts/viewport and disable only irrelevant nondeterministic animation in visual fixtures, never production security behavior.
- [ ] UX-008-T-04: Capture exact revision, commands, counts/skips/failures, artifacts and acceptance decision in the consolidated report; retain failed evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- UX-008-AC-01: Every PRD change passes TypeScript, lint, unit, relevant integration, affected Playwright, role, responsive, accessibility and existing regression gates before merge.
- UX-008-AC-02: Shared shell/token changes trigger all affected consumers and required full release regression; targeted development tests do not replace that gate.
- UX-008-AC-03: Visual diffs require explicit review; changes cannot be approved by silently regenerating baselines, skipping tests or relaxing assertions.
- UX-008-AC-04: A failure is recorded with scope/cause/impact/owner/disposition and rerun evidence; unknown or blocked checks cannot count as passed or accepted.

## Automated tests

- UX-008-TC-01: Source/CI guards: verify-browser-shards.mjs and verify-integration-suites.mjs plus relevant contract tests.
- UX-008-TC-02: Playwright/Axe: controlled and real-service scenarios, role denials, responsive/reflow and approved screenshot fixtures.
- UX-008-TC-03: Negative checks: prove omitted required suite, changed baseline or swallowed failure cannot satisfy acceptance; current immutable release evidence remains required.
